followups_sent.step: Can you write a four-bar intro that leads into the verse progression?

text:
Here is a 4-bar intro in A major that leads into the verse. It uses a simple I–V–IV–V progression, building gently toward the A chord in bar 1 of the verse.

LH (4 bars, 3 pipes):

A2 w (5) | E3 w (1) | D3 w (5) | E3 w (1)

RH (4 bars, 3 pipes):

pp "dolce" V1: A4 h (1), E5 h (3) | rit. G#4 h (1), B4 h (3) | F#4 h (1), A4 h (3) | a tempo G#4 h (1), B4 h (3)
V2: r w | r w | r w | r w

Pedal line:

Ped. ______________________________________________________________ *

The intro starts quietly on pp with A major, moves to the dominant E, steps down to D for warmth, then returns to E as the pickup into the verse. The "dolce" marking keeps the tone gentle. The rit. in bar 2 creates a brief pause before the subdominant color in bar 3, and "a tempo" in bar 4 brings the pulse back as the verse begins.
